title: Getting Started with gghoneycomb
text: honeycomb layout useful showing proportional abundance categories. example, visualize pollen composition honey sample.
code: library(ggplot2) library(gghoneycomb) pollen <- data.frame(   species = c("Clover", "Wildflower", "Lavender", "Sunflower", "Other"),   count = c(45, 25, 15, 10, 5) )  ggplot(pollen, aes(fill = species, weight = count)) +   geom_honeycomb(n_cells = 80, compaction = 0.9, seed = 123) +   scale_fill_honey() +   theme_honeycomb() +   coord_equal() #> Warning: Computation failed in `stat_honeycomb()`. #> Caused by error in `allocate_regions()`: #> ! Frontier exhausted for category 'Wildflower': allocated 18 of 20 cells. Consider increasing grid size or adjusting category proportions.

title: Getting Started with gghoneycomb
text: provide n_cells, gghoneycomb chooses value based number categories smallest proportion. rule thumb, cell counts 50 500 tend work well plots; higher values increase detail can make small regions harder see.
code: ggplot(pollen, aes(fill = species, weight = count)) +   geom_honeycomb(compaction = 1) +   scale_fill_honey() +   theme_honeycomb() +   coord_equal() #> Warning: Computation failed in `stat_honeycomb()`. #> Caused by error in `allocate_regions()`: #> ! Frontier exhausted for category 'Other': allocated 4 of 5 cells. Consider increasing grid size or adjusting category proportions.

title: Getting Started with gghoneycomb
text: already proportions, set values_are = "proportions" pass values via weight aesthetic.
code: pollen_prop <- data.frame(   species = c("Clover", "Wildflower", "Lavender", "Sunflower", "Other"),   prop = c(0.45, 0.25, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05) )  ggplot(pollen_prop, aes(fill = species, weight = prop)) +   geom_honeycomb(values_are = "proportions", n_cells = 80, seed = 123) +   scale_fill_honey(direction = -1) +   theme_honeycomb() +   coord_equal() #> Warning: Computation failed in `stat_honeycomb()`. #> Caused by error in `allocate_regions()`: #> ! Frontier exhausted for category 'Sunflower': allocated 7 of 8 cells. Consider increasing grid size or adjusting category proportions.

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
text: geom_honeycomb() creates honeycomb-style waffle chart hexagonal cells represent proportional data. category forms contiguous region connected hexagons, making easy compare relative sizes.

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
code: geom_honeycomb(   mapping = NULL,   data = NULL,   stat = "honeycomb",   position = "identity",   na.rm = FALSE,   show.legend = NA,   inherit.aes = TRUE,   values_are = c("auto", "counts", "proportions"),   n_cells = NULL,   compaction = 1,   min_width = NULL,   max_width = NULL,   min_height = NULL,   max_height = NULL,   seed = NULL,   ... )

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
text: mapping Set aesthetic mappings created ggplot2::aes(). Required: fill (category) weight (numeric values). data data displayed layer. stat statistical transformation use data. Default "honeycomb". position Position adjustment, either string result position adjustment function. typically used honeycomb plots. na.rm FALSE, default, missing values removed warning. TRUE, missing values silently removed. show.legend Logical. layer included legends? inherit.aes FALSE, overrides default aesthetics rather combining . values_are interpret weight aesthetic values: "auto" (Default) weights sum 1 (within tolerance 1e-6), treat proportions; otherwise treat counts. "counts" Treat weights raw counts normalized. "proportions" Treat weights proportions (must sum 1). n_cells Number hexagonal cells use. NULL (default), automatically chosen based number categories minimum proportion. Maximum allowed 2500. compaction Controls regularity honeycomb boundary: 1 (Default) Rectangular bounding grid. < 1 Increasingly irregular silhouette via boundary erosion. Must range (0, 1]. min_width, max_width Constraints grid width (number columns). Default NULL means constraint. min_height, max_height Constraints grid height (number rows). Default NULL means constraint. seed Random seed reproducible layouts compaction < 1. NULL, uses random seed. ... arguments passed ggplot2::layer().

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
text: ggplot2 layer can added plot.

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
text: geom_honeycomb() understands following aesthetics: Required aesthetics: fill categorical variable defining groups. unique value gets contiguous region hexagonal cells. weight Numeric values representing counts proportions category. determine many cells category receives. aesthetic required geom error provided. Optional aesthetics: colour Border color hexagonal cells. Default NA (border). alpha Transparency fill color. Default 1 (opaque). linewidth Width cell borders. Default 0.5. (Note: visible colour set.) linetype Type cell borders. Default 1 (solid). Ignored aesthetics: x, y ignored honeycomb layout computed internally based weights. need () map variables x y.

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
text: values_are parameter controls weight values interpreted: "auto" (default) weights sum 1 (within tolerance 1e-6), treated proportions. Otherwise, treated counts normalized internally. "counts" Weights raw counts (e.g., 40, 30, 20, 10). normalized proportions internally. "proportions" Weights proportions must sum 1 (e.g., 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1). error raised .

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
text: honeycomb layout ensures: category forms exactly one contiguous region (connected hexagons) Cell counts proportional weights (using largest-remainder rounding) Every non-zero category gets least one cell Layouts reproducible seed set

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
text: stat computes tooltip_label pct, can used optional interactive backends ggiraph. Keep core plots static; need tooltips, can layer ggiraph::geom_polygon_interactive() map ggplot2::after_stat(tooltip_label).

title: Honeycomb waffle chart — geom_honeycomb
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(ggplot2)  # Basic honeycomb with counts pollen_data <- data.frame(   species = c("Clover", "Wildflower", "Lavender", "Sunflower", "Other"),   count = c(45, 25, 15, 10, 5) )  ggplot(pollen_data, aes(fill = species, weight = count)) +   geom_honeycomb() +   coord_equal()  # With proportions (explicit) pollen_prop <- data.frame(   species = c("Clover", "Wildflower", "Lavender", "Sunflower", "Other"),   prop = c(0.45, 0.25, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05) )  ggplot(pollen_prop, aes(fill = species, weight = prop)) +   geom_honeycomb(values_are = "proportions") +   coord_equal()  # Control cell count and layout ggplot(pollen_data, aes(fill = species, weight = count)) +   geom_honeycomb(n_cells = 50, compaction = 0.8, seed = 42) +   coord_equal()  # Optional tooltip usage with ggiraph if (requireNamespace("ggiraph", quietly = TRUE)) {   ggplot(pollen_data, aes(fill = species, weight = count)) +     ggiraph::geom_polygon_interactive(       stat = "honeycomb",       aes(tooltip = ggplot2::after_stat(tooltip_label))     ) +     coord_equal() }  # With grid constraints ggplot(pollen_data, aes(fill = species, weight = count)) +   geom_honeycomb(min_width = 8, max_width = 12) +   coord_equal() } # }
